note: Items have either an ASIN (a specific product) or a search (an Amazon search link with the Store ID). The searches are placeholders until the owner picks specific products; swap "search" for "asin" to link one. "keys" match the shopping list in the report (trebgen.hardware.bill_of_materials).

starterKit.title: Supplies for the desk trebuchet
starterKit.intro: Everything else is printed: the kit snaps together with no screws or bolts. This is what the default trebuchet still needs (the counterweight is coins from a jar).

items.why: The sling cords: strong and doesn't stretch.
The trigger cord, so you fire from beside the machine.
Weigh the coins for the counterweight.

categories.title: Axle upgrades (optional)
categories.intro: The kit needs no hardware: the axle and hinge are printed snap pins. For a smoother, stronger axle, pick the M8 bolt option in the designer, and add two 608 skateboard bearings for the smoothest swing.

items.name: 608 bearings (8 × 22 × 7 mm)
items.note: Only with the bearing option. Get the sealed (2RS) kind; you need two.

items.search: M8 hex bolts nylon lock nuts washers kit
items.name: M8 bolts, lock nuts and washers
items.note: Only with the M8 axle options. The report says how long; longer is fine with a washer stack.

categories.title: Sling and trigger
categories.intro: The pouch, release ring and trigger pin are printed. You need string for the two sling cords and a cord to pull the trigger from a safe distance.

items.name: Braided fishing line, 20 lb or more
items.note: Thin, strong and barely stretches, so the release is repeatable.

items.name: Nylon twine or kite string
items.note: About 1 m, tied to the trigger pin's ring so you fire from beside the machine. Any strong string works.

items.name: Leather craft scraps (optional)
items.note: If you'd rather have a soft pouch than the printed one: cut 30 × 60 mm and punch a hole at each end.

items.name: Small split rings, 10–12 mm (optional)
items.note: A metal ring slides off the release hook a little more cleanly than the printed one.

categories.title: Counterweight fill
categories.intro: The heavier the fill for its size, the smaller the bucket. Weigh it on a kitchen scale.

items.name: Steel BBs (4.5 mm)
items.note: Densest easy fill, and they pour. About 350 g fills the default bucket.

items.name: Steel nuts, bulk
items.note: A box of nuts makes a tidy, reusable counterweight.

items.name: Play sand
items.note: Cheap but light, so the bucket comes out bigger.

items.name: Digital kitchen scale
items.note: To weigh the fill (coins too) and your projectiles: the estimate is only as good as the numbers.

categories.title: Things to throw
categories.intro: Light and round goes farthest. The kit includes a printable ball; these are the other choices in the designer.

items.name: Small foam balls
items.note: Safe indoors.

items.name: Ping-pong balls
items.note: Light and big: they slow down fast in the air. Fun indoors.

items.name: Glass marbles (16 mm)
items.note: Heavy and fast. Outdoors only, with a clear field.

items.name: Mini marshmallows
items.note: The classic desk-trebuchet ammo.

categories.title: Filament
categories.intro: What I print with. The whole default trebuchet takes about 220 g. Sunlu, 1.75 mm, 1 kg spools; other colours are on each listing.

items.name: Sunlu PLA, 1 kg
items.note: Easiest to print and stiff: right for the frames and trough.

items.name: Sunlu PLA+ 2.0, 1 kg
items.note: Tougher PLA. Good for the arm, which takes the most force.

items.name: Sunlu PETG, 1 kg
items.note: Tougher still and less brittle, if your arm or bucket ears crack.

categories.title: Safety and testing
categories.intro: Glasses for the throw, and a tape to measure it: compare your throws with the estimate.

items.name: Safety glasses
items.note: Impact-rated, for everyone near the throw.

items.name: Long measuring tape
items.note: Measure from the axle to where it lands. Try five throws and take the middle one.

items.name: Screwdriver and spanner set
items.note: For the M3 screws and the lock nuts.
